method: PCA(n_components=0.95) then KMeans(n_clusters=3) on flattened grayscale training crops; anomaly score is Euclidean distance to the nearest cluster centroid
selection_rule: mean + 2*std of the validation distance distribution, read off the histogram by inspection (no grid search, no cross-validation, test split not used)
degradation_probe_note: measured, not assumed: a strong brightness shift (severe darkening, overexposure) or a glare-like patch moves the distance far from every training centroid and is reliably caught; moderate blur and a small solid occlusion barely move it, and blur can pull it slightly closer to a centroid -- raw-pixel Euclidean distance is dominated by overall intensity level, not the fine edge detail blur destroys or a patch covers
recognition_error_note: spot-checking flagged crops by eye, most remain readable to a person -- the gate is not a human-readability detector. Cross-checking against the fused recognizer's own correctness instead (not just a visual impression) shows flagged crops do carry a meaningfully higher model error rate, with a roughly monotonic trend across distance quintiles -- so the flag tracks 'the model is more likely to be wrong here', not 'a human would refuse to read this'
limitations: raw-pixel PCA+KMeans distance is primarily a brightness/exposure and gross-appearance anomaly detector, not a general catch-all: it does not reliably catch blur or small occlusions (see degradation_probe). It also does not detect human-unreadability -- flagged crops are mostly still legible by eye (see recognition_error_note); what it tracks is atypicality relative to the training distribution, which happens to correlate with higher model error but is a different thing from photo quality as a person would judge it, so a 'retake recommended' message overstates what is known. It cannot say why a crop was flagged, and with no labelled quality data the threshold rests on visual inspection of the validation histogram, not measured precision/recall against real bad photos
